findings.summary: to_str().unwrap() panics and crashes the entire Node.js process when HTML input contains non-UTF-8 byte sequences
findings.failure_scenario: A scraped web page serves HTML with an encoding mis-declared as UTF-8 but containing Latin-1 bytes in the 0x80-0xFF range. The scraper's HTTP client decodes it into a JS string with replacement characters, but if the actual response bytes are passed directly as a C string through koffi FFI, to_str() fails and the entire service process terminates.

findings.summary: CString::new().unwrap() panics and crashes the Node.js process if a base href attribute contains an embedded null byte
findings.failure_scenario: A malicious or corrupted HTML page contains <base href="https://example.com/\x00evil">. The scraper extracts the href value containing the null byte, CString::new() panics, and the entire service process terminates.

findings.summary: extractLinksRust parses the same HTML twice (once to extract links, once to extract base href), each via a separate parse_html() call in Rust
findings.failure_scenario: On the scrape hot path with large HTML documents (e.g., 500KB+ pages), the duplicate full-HTML parse doubles CPU time spent in the Rust HTML parser, adding measurable latency per scrape. A single combined Rust function returning both links and base href would parse once.
